title: Proposing-Side Optimal Stable Matching
body_html:
Proposing-Side Optimal Stable Matching

Theorem. Let $\mu^M$ denote the matching produced by the men-proposing Gale-Shapley algorithm on $(M, W, \succ)$. Then:

  1. Men-optimal. For every man $i \in M$ and every stable matching $\mu$:

$$\mu^M(i) \succeq_i \mu(i)$$

I.e., every man weakly prefers his match in $\mu^M$ to his match in any other stable matching.

  1. Women-pessimal. For every woman $j \in W$ and every stable matching $\mu$:

$$\mu(j) \succeq_j \mu^M(j)$$

I.e., every woman weakly prefers her match in any other stable matching to her match in $\mu^M$.

A symmetric pair of statements holds for the women-proposing algorithm with roles swapped.
proof_html:
Sketch

Call a man-woman pair $(i, j)$ achievable if some stable matching matches $i$ to $j$.

Men-optimal (claim 1): By induction on the round of the men-proposing algorithm, no man $i$ is ever rejected by an achievable partner. The inductive step uses the structure of stable matchings: if $i$ were rejected by an achievable partner $j$, then $j$ would be holding some preferred $i'$ who, in any stable matching pairing $i$ with $j$, would block — contradiction.

Hence at the end, each man $i$ is matched (or stays single) with the best-for-him achievable partner; that is his match in $\mu^M$.

Women-pessimal (claim 2): If a woman $j$ were strictly better off in $\mu^M$ than in some stable $\mu$, then she would have $\mu^M(j) = i$ with $i \succ_j \mu^{-1}(j)$. By claim 1, $\mu^M(i) \succeq_i \mu(i)$, so $j \succeq_i \mu(i)$. Combining gives a blocking pair $(i, j)$ for $\mu$ — contradicting stability of $\mu$.

Consequences

The set of stable matchings has a distinguished extremal element on each side. Combined with the [[lattice]] structure, this gives an explicit characterization of the boundary of the stable set.

References

  • [MSZ Ch.22, Thm 22.11] Maschler, Solan, Zamir, Game Theory.
  • Gale & Shapley (1962), original optimality observation.
  • Roth & Sotomayor (1990), Two-Sided Matching, Ch. 2.
